papers.title: Diffusion Sensitivity Geometry and Strong Duality for Optimal Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs
papers.abstract: Existing approaches to differential privacy in diffusion models rely on loose sensitivity bounds and isotropic Gaussian noise, leading to unnecessary estimation error. We develop a framework for the optimal privacy-utility tradeoff of ideal diffusion denoisers, replacing conservative bounds with exact sensitivity characterizations and provably optimal noise calibration. First, we show that worst-case sensitivity over datasets of arbitrary size can be characterized exactly using only two records. For a data domain of size $m$, this reduces the analysis to at most $m(m-1)$ constraints, regardless of dataset size. Our characterization can be arbitrarily tighter than conventional diameter-based sensitivity bounds, revealing potentially unbounded improvements in noise calibration. Second, we obtain exact privacy guarantees for R\'enyi, approximate, and Gaussian differential privacy, as well as mutual-information privacy for binary records, avoiding the looseness of previous generic privacy conversions. Finally, we show that the minimum achievable weighted mean-squared error can be computed through a semidefinite program and prove strong duality, providing certificates of global optimality.

papers.title: Optimal R\'enyi and Logarithmic Additive Functional Entropy Estimation
papers.abstract: We characterize the minimax sample complexity of estimating R\'enyi entropy from independent samples on an alphabet of size at most $k$, when the known order $\alpha>1$ may vary with $k$. For every fixed additive accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and success probability $2/3$, we prove matching bounds with constants independent of $k$ and $\alpha$. For $1<\alpha<\log k$, the rate is $\Theta_\varepsilon(\alpha k^{1-1/\alpha}X_\alpha(k,\varepsilon))$, where a monotone scalar inequality defines $X_\alpha$ at noninteger orders. The bounds remain uniform as the order approaches one or an integer, or grows with the alphabet. Integer orders below $\log k$ have rate $\Theta_\varepsilon(\alpha k^{1-1/\alpha})$; orders at least $\log k$ and min-entropy have rate $\Theta_\varepsilon(k\log k)$. We extend the analysis to logarithms of positive additive functionals. For every fixed continuous $f$ satisfying $f(0)=0$, $f(x)>0$ for $x>0$, and $f(x)\sim ax^r$ at zero, with $a>0$ and $r>1$, estimating $-\beta^{-1}\log\sum_i f(p_i)$ at fixed accuracy, for fixed $\beta>0$, has sample complexity $\Theta(k^{1-1/r})$ for integer $r$ and $\Theta(k/\log k)$ otherwise. A replication reduction preserves the sampling experiment and transfers the rates for powers. Smooth flat functions show that regularity alone does not determine the complexity. The upper bound combines polynomial approximation, Gamma count statistics, and an independent pilot, with a global affine correction near order one. The lower bound uses interpolation to construct positive mean-one priors and controls their distinguishability and entropy separation after normalization. Exact count-variance identities and weighted approximation duality connect the two arguments.

papers.title: PQ-Vault: Provably Quantum-Safe Asset Custody for Unmodified Ethereum
papers.abstract: A quantum computer could recover the key of any Ethereum account whose public key appears on chain. We prove that no sidechain or bridge that leaves Ethereum's rules unchanged can protect such accounts: their funds must move into a contract whose release condition relies only on quantum-safe primitives. We design \emph{PQ-Vault}, a custody system for unmodified Ethereum combining this vault, a quantum-safe proof-of-stake sidechain whose checkpoints carry compact certificates, and an optimistic dispute protocol. We give the first security proof of compact certificates against quantum attackers and a matching attack: with classically chosen parameters, the guarantee falls from 128 to about 60 bits, and a simple rule restores it. We show that a common seed-update rule in hash-chain proof of stake lets an attacker steer chosen slots and profit from splitting its stake, and give an election whose steering gain and inclusion delay are provably bounded against quantum attackers. Since compressing certificates with a pairing-based SNARK breaks quantum security, we use fraud proofs that need a single signature check. For 65,536 validators, a certificate is 0.8 MB, 260 times smaller than all signatures, and verifies in about 20 ms; the vault accepts a checkpoint for about 420,000 gas.

papers.title: Learning to Interfere in Non-Orthogonal Multiple-Access Joint Source-Channel Coding
papers.abstract: We consider multiple transmitters aiming to communicate their source signals (e.g., images) over a multiple access channel (MAC). Conventional communication systems minimize interference by orthogonally allocating resources (time and/or bandwidth) among users, which limits their capacity. We introduce a machine learning (ML)-aided wireless image transmission method that merges compression and channel coding using a multi-view autoencoder, which allows the transmitters to use all the available channel resources simultaneously, resulting in a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme. The receiver must recover all the images from the received superposed signal, while also associating each image with its transmitter. Traditional ML models deal with individual samples, whereas our model allows signals from different users to interfere in order to leverage gains from NOMA under limited bandwidth and power constraints. We introduce a progressive fine-tuning algorithm that doubles the number of users at each iteration, maintaining initial performance with orthogonalized user-specific projections, which is then improved through fine-tuning steps. Remarkably, our method supports up to 64 users with potential for further scaling, with only a 2.4% increase in the number of trainable parameters compared to a single-user model, significantly enhancing recovered image quality and outperforming existing NOMA-based methods over a wide range of datasets, metrics, and channel conditions. Our approach paves the way for more efficient and robust multi-user communication systems, leveraging innovative ML components and strategies.

papers.title: Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory
papers.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitors are LLM-based systems that analyze reasoning traces to detect when outputs may exhibit attributes of interest, such as test-hacking behavior during code generation. In this paper, we use information-theoretic analysis to show that non-zero mutual information between CoT and output is a necessary but not sufficient condition for CoT monitorability. We identify two sources of approximation error that may undermine the performance of CoT monitors in practice: information gap, which measures the extent to which the monitor can extract the information available in CoT, and elicitation error, which measures the extent to which the monitor approximates the optimal monitoring function. Empirically, we show that CoT obfuscation can arise even in the absence of any optimization pressure against CoT. We further demonstrate that the fragility of CoT monitorability can be systematically mitigated through targeted training objectives. To this end, we propose a practical, label-free objective based on mutual information between outputs and CoTs, and benchmark it against an oracle-based method that directly rewards the monitored model for CoTs that maximize monitor accuracy. Across multiple environments, we show that our objective is effective at preventing CoT obfuscation even when training against a monitor, and helps mitigate reward hacking when the task reward is imperfectly specified.

papers.title: Asymmetric Likelihood-Free Hypothesis Testing
papers.abstract: In likelihood-free hypothesis testing (LFHT), given samples from two unknown distributions $P,Q$ on $[n]$ with $\mathrm{d_{TV}}(P,Q)\geq\varepsilon$, and from a third distribution $D\in\{P,Q\}$, the goal is to identify whether $D=P$ or $D=Q$. We study asymmetric likelihood-free hypothesis testing, where the sample budgets $s_P$ and $s_Q$ for $P$ and $Q$ may differ, and characterize the feasible triples $(s_P,s_Q,s_D)$ up to logarithmic factors. We establish that unequal reference budgets can give a polynomial saving. For instance, for constant separation, $n$ samples from $P$ and $n^{3/4}$ from $Q$ allow testing with $\widetilde O(n^{1/4})$ samples from $D$, whereas both existing baselines---symmetric LFHT and unequal-sample closeness testing---require $\Omega(\sqrt n)$ samples from $D$. We further apply our results to non-adaptive distribution 2-clustering, where the sample allocation among $k$ distributions must be fixed before observing any data. We obtain matching upper and lower bounds for this problem up to logarithmic factors in terms of the domain size, number of distributions, smaller cluster size, and separation, both with one cluster distribution known and with both unknown. Comparing with known bounds for adaptive sample allocation gives a worst-case adaptivity gap of $\widetilde\Theta(k^{1/4})$.

papers.title: Moment Ambiguity and the Limits of Robust Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We study fundamental information-theoretic limits of robust stochastic optimization when the distribution is known only through its exact moment sequence. We develop a unified framework that produces families of distinct distributions sharing all moments yet inducing radically different optimal decisions, thereby establishing strong impossibility results for a range of decision problems under moment ambiguity. Our binary and $N$-way moment-matching constructions separate quantiles, threshold regions, and online selection opportunities while preserving every moment. For the newsvendor problem, moment equivalence causes quantile ambiguity, inducing any fixed or randomized order quantity to fail arbitrarily badly. For revenue maximization, no deterministic or randomized posted pricing scheme can secure a nontrivial approximation relative to the full-information benchmark. For the secretary problem with cardinal observations, the optimal robust success probability under exact moment disclosure is the classical finite-horizon value $s_m$, even for i.i.d. observations. This value converges to $1/e$, compared with the full-information limit of approximately $0.5801$ due to Gilbert and Mosteller (J. Am. Stat. Assoc., 1966). We also recover and expand upon the recent impossibility result of Correa et al. (STOC, 2026) for prophet inequalities with moment knowledge. For every fixed $r\ge1$, exact moment knowledge can yield at best a $\Theta(1/\log m)$ competitive ratio, even when competing against relaxed benchmarks based on expected $r$-th order statistics or when the algorithm is allowed to select $r$ items.

papers.title: A Matroidal Framework for Random Access in Linear Codes
papers.abstract: We study random access in linear codes when codeword symbols are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement. A code is recovery balanced if the expected number of samples required to recover a codeword coordinate is the same for every coordinate. We express the recovery expectations in terms of the associated matroid and derive a coordinatewise identity relating these values for a code and its dual. This proves that a linear code is recovery balanced if and only if its dual is recovery balanced, establishing a conjecture of Gruica et al. We further define the recovery balance for arbitrary matroids and show that asymptotically almost every sparse paving matroid is not recovery balanced.

papers.title: Universality of approximate message passing under a fourth-moment tail condition
papers.abstract: We prove state evolution for approximate message passing (AMP) with rectangular random matrices whose entries are independent, centered, and variance-normalized. The row and column dimensions grow with a ratio that converges to a positive finite limit. The entry laws may differ across coordinates and dimensions, and we assume uniform integrability of the fourth powers of the rescaled entries. For entries sampled independently from a fixed law, a finite fourth moment suffices, with no requirement for higher moments. The nonlinearities are continuously differentiable and globally Lipschitz, with bounded continuous first state derivatives. The signal and noise have independent and identically distributed coordinates with finite moments of all orders, and are independent of each other and of the matrix. At every fixed number of iterations, empirical averages of pseudo-Lipschitz functions of order two converge in probability to the limits specified by Gaussian state evolution. These averages include empirical second moments and products of trajectory coordinates. The proof combines an aggregate bound on third derivatives with randomized Lindeberg replacement and operator-norm truncation, without matching third moments or invoking a non-Gaussian universality theorem. We also show that independence of complementary projected components for every deterministic rank-one constraint pair characterizes Gaussian entries. This identifies the limitation of extending Gaussian conditioning identities to independent non-Gaussian matrices. Finally, a variance-profile example shows that average variance normalization alone does not ensure the homogeneous state evolution limits.

papers.title: From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Many problems in signal processing, machine learning, and neuroimaging provide several jointly observed measurements of one process, each mixing a component common to all of them with a component private to itself, and require the common component to be recovered without supervision. This problem has been studied in several communities, largely independently. Statisticians proposed canonical correlation analysis (CCA), introduced by Hotelling in 1936. Information theorists proposed two notions of common information, due to G\'acs and K\"orner and to Wyner. Engineers developed subspace methods for sensor arrays and multiuser communications to design multiview receivers. This tutorial presents the main results and tools each community developed for this problem in a single exposition, and explains the connections that emerge where they meet, distinguishing exact equivalences from special cases and analogies. We develop the information-theoretic foundation from first principles. We then introduce CCA and its extension to several views, followed by the engineering thread from blind multiuser detection to CCA as a blind receiver. Next, we turn to nonlinear CCA, covering kernel, deep, and probabilistic formulations, the conditions under which the common factor is identifiable, and connections to self-supervised learning. We conclude with a discussion of further extensions and open directions. The exposition is self-contained, so that readers from each of these communities can follow the parts developed by the others.

papers.title: Encoding Trees: A Method for Producing a Variable-Length Prefix Code From Sets of Arbitrary Size
papers.abstract: In this work we formalize a new class of binary trees called encoding trees. We extend this structure in two ways, through labelling to create the class of labelled encoding trees, and pruning to create the class of pruned encoding trees. We discuss how these two extensions can be combined to create the the class of pruned labelled encoding trees. Using the supplementary results that we prove about these classes of trees, we construct a code that uses pruned labelled encoding trees to convert a string of symbols from a sequence of non-empty sets to a binary string. We prove that this code is a variable-length prefix code that can process any valid string of symbols from the given sequence of non-empty sets. Furthermore, we construct a code from the class of pruned labelled encoding trees that goes in the opposite direction, from binary strings to a string of symbols from a sequence of non-empty sets of arbitrary symbols. We prove that this code is also a variable-length prefix code that can process any binary string of any length, provided that the sequence of non-empty sets is sufficiently long. We provide an equation that establishes the minimum sequence length to encode any binary string of a given length, based on that length.

papers.title: From Linear Exact Repair to Mixed-Alphabet Codes: The Bandwidth-Subpacketization Tradeoff of MDS Array Codes
papers.abstract: MDS array codes achieve optimal storage efficiency in distributed storage systems, but their repair bandwidth depends critically on the sub-packetization level. While the theoretically optimal repair bandwidth (i.e., cut-set bound) of a high-rate exact-repair MDS array code is attainable with sufficiently large sub-packetization, the fundamental limits for fixed sub-packetization remain poorly understood. We study this problem for centralized linear exact repair of $h$ failures from $d$ helper nodes over a fixed finite field. We show that the rank profile of any linear repair scheme is constrained by two auxiliary mixed-alphabet codes. The first code is formed from the kernels of the helper projections and exists for all repair degrees; the second is formed from their row spaces and applies in the full-helper regime when $d\ge r$. These codes have complementary alphabet profiles, and their size and minimum-distance requirements are forced solely by the MDS property and repair correctness. This gives a unified route from classical coding-theoretic upper bounds to repair-bandwidth lower bounds. As a consequence, we obtain several explicit lower bounds via Singleton, Hamming, Plotkin, and Griesmer arguments, including known bounds as corollaries. We further formulate a Delsarte-type support-enumerator LP for mixed-alphabet codes and give an exact type-compressed implementation. For fixed sub-packetization \(\ell\), this yields a polynomial-time procedure for evaluating the resulting finite-parameter lower bound.

papers.title: Support periods of polynomials and support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes over Galois rings
papers.abstract: Let \(A=\GR(p^e,r)\) have residue field \(\F_q\), and let \(\lambda\in A^\times\). We relate coefficient compression of monic divisors of \(X^N-\lambda\) to support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes. At a simple-root length, the support period of every nonconstant monic divisor is preserved at each coefficient precision and equals the order of the multiplicative stabilizer of its root set. For a cyclic Frobenius-orbit polynomial, the multiple equal-difference structure determines its support period, core degree, and least relative degree of an unramified extension over which all its basic-irreducible factors are binomials. Coordinate projections give every constacyclic code over a finite commutative ring a unique maximal interleaving into copies of one support-primitive code. At simple-root lengths over \(A\), the intrinsic period of a code is the greatest common divisor of the periods of its torsion codes. The decomposition yields distance and duality formulas and the arithmetic Singleton bound for free codes. At every length, a nonzero code over \(A\) has the same minimum Hamming distance as its highest torsion code, which gives a refined bound. At repeated-root lengths, identical torsion filtrations can occur with different intrinsic periods, while a class of nonzero codes obtained by substitution from simple-root generators retains the same core and minimum distance. Trace matrices recover the coefficients of basic-irreducible cores using unit pivots, and local Hensel corrections lift compressed factors directly. For \(X^n-1\) with \(p\nmid n\), lifting and output have quasi-linear bit cost in the compressed representation when the arithmetic data and residue factorizations are given.

papers.title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design for MIMO-ISAC
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.

papers.title: Generalization Bounds via Vector-Valued $L_p$ Correlation $V_\alpha$
papers.abstract: Understanding generalization of randomized learning algorithms remains a central challenge. Mutual-information and total-variation bounds provide complementary ways to quantify data--hypothesis dependence, but they can behave quite differently in high-dimensional regimes. We study a one-parameter family of dependence measures, the vector-valued $L_p$-norm correlation $V_\alpha$, and derive generalization bounds whose dependence terms interpolate between total variation (TV) at $\alpha=1$ and variance and $\chi^2$ related behavior at $\alpha=2$. For $\alpha>2$, the H\"older-conjugate loss moment is below two, yielding heavy-tailed specializations that can remain finite even when the loss variance is infinite. A particularly interpretable specialization occurs at $\alpha=2$, where the bound can be expressed in terms of the variability of the algorithm's output density across datasets, $\int \sqrt{\mathrm{Var}_S[p(w\mid S)]}~ dw$. We show that the entire $V_\alpha$ family is invariant under smooth bijective reparameterizations of the hypothesis space. We also introduce an adaptive density stability (ADS) condition that implies explicit control of $V_2$, and we verify it for Gibbs-type posteriors under bounded losses (yielding rates that depend on the inverse temperature and sample size). To address scaling, we extend the framework to a conditional formulation using supersamples, analogous in spirit to conditional mutual information (CMI), and discuss evaluations in the output space as a practical surrogate for estimating dependence. Simulations on Bayesian linear regression illustrate how tuning $\alpha$ can change the tightness of the resulting bounds across regimes. Additional supersample experiments on noisy MNIST and on a pretrained ResNet-50 for CIFAR-10 show similar behavior of the projected loss-space bounds beyond the original clean-MNIST setting.

papers.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q>19683$, we settle the Cheng--Murray deep-hole problem for full-length Reed--Solomon codes in every dimension $2\le k\le q-2$, with the characteristic-two cases stated explicitly. For odd $q$, the deep holes are precisely the words of degree $k$. For even $q$ and $k\ge3$, the same conclusion holds except for an additional family when $k=q-3$. In even characteristic and dimension two, every deep hole has a unique expression $a h(X)+bX+c$, where $a\ne0$ and $h$ is a normalized $o$-polynomial. The proof combines quadratic quotient algebras, graph-theoretic weighted independent-set inequalities, and planar arc completion. We also obtain normal rational curve rigidity in the corresponding nonexceptional dimensions, the projective Reed--Solomon covering radii, and distinct-coordinate solvability and remainder criteria.

papers.title: Exploiting Pinching Antenna Systems in NOMA Covert Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) provide flexible transmitter-side radiation reconfiguration for high-frequency wireless communications. This paper applies PASS to non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) covert communication networks, where activated pinching antennas (PAs) transmit superimposed signals to a pair of users stochastically distributed within a rectangle. Two passive wardens respectively monitor the downlink transmissions intended for two users. More specifically, we derive the closed-form detection error probability (DEP) expressions for two wardens under bounded noise uncertainty. Then we analytically determine the optimal detection thresholds and minimum DEPs in the worst-case covert detection scenarios. The covert transmission rates of two users are further characterized by taking into consideration ideal successive interference cancellation and non-ideal successive interference cancellation at near user and intra-NOMA interference at far user. Numerical results are presented to confirm that: 1) PASS-NOMA is capable of providing higher covert rates relative to conventional orthogonal multiple access OMA schemes; 2) As the number of activated PAs begun to increase, the near user has ability to obtain a larger covert rate gain than far user; and 3) The DEP of PASS-NOMA networks is larger than that of both PASS-OMA and traditional antenna (TA) based NOMA in specific output power regions.

papers.title: Point Cloud Transmission With Patch-Based Rate Adaptation
papers.abstract: We propose a joint source-channel coding (JSCC) framework for efficient wireless point cloud transmission. In the proposed scheme, the point cloud is first divided into local patches and transformed into compact latent representations, which are then mapped to symbols for transmission over a noisy channel. Our model incorporates an entropy model that exploits inter-patch spatial dependencies to estimate patch-level coding costs and allocate different numbers of symbols accordingly. Unlike existing patch-based point cloud JSCC methods that use the same transmission rate between patches, we adapt the channel usage of each patch latent representation. To exploit inter-patch dependencies without patch-by-patch autoregressive processing, we select a group of anchor patches whose features provide contextual information for entropy estimation of non-anchor ones. The framework is trained using a reconstruction loss and an entropy-based rate surrogate. Experiments on ModelNet40 demonstrate overall rate-distortion improvements over existing baselines across channel conditions.

papers.title: Broadcasting in Centimeter-Wave Gigantic MIMO Systems: Beam Shaping is All You Need
papers.abstract: Beamforming is a key enabling technology for centimeter-wave Gigantic MIMO (G-MIMO) systems, using antenna arrays to generate wide beams for cell-wide broadcasting or narrow beams for data transmission. This paper presents a novel \emph{beam shaping technology} for designing environment-aware broadcast beams (i.e., beams for common control information delivery, as in 5G SSB). As a case study, we shape a \emph{prostrate beam} in the vertical plane to approximate uniform electromagnetic power distribution across the ground, thereby enhancing broadcast coverage quality. We first propose a geometric broadcasting model that, through coordinate transformation, relates base station height, beam spread, maximum service distance, and downtilt angle. Building on this model and the signal propagation model, we formulate the beam shaping problem as a non-convex optimization problem that aims to maximize ground-level coverage. To solve it, we develop a generalized optimization framework. We reformulate the problem into a matrix representation, equivalently transforming it into a target pursuit optimization (TPO) problem. Using variable substitution, the objective is convexified into a quadratically constrained quadratic program, and the non-convex rank constraint is handled via successive convex approximation, decomposing the problem into iteratively solved subproblems. We provide complexity and convergence analyses for the proposed algorithm. Numerical simulations confirm that the optimization effectively shapes the intended beam pattern and that the proposed prostrate beam yields significant performance gains, including substantially extended coverage distance, over conventional wide-beam benchmarks.

papers.title: Matrix $\Phi$-Entropic Measures of Dependence
papers.abstract: We introduce matrix $\Phi$-ribbons, extending the scalar $\Phi$-ribbons to the matrix case. For $\Phi$ in the subadditivity class, we establish data processing and tensorization properties of matrix $\Phi$-ribbons. We establish scalar and matrix $\Phi$-entropy inequalities and use them to show that both $\Phi$-ribbons characterize the corresponding $\Phi$-strong data processing inequality (SDPI) constants. We obtain exact evaluations of the SDPI constants for several sources. We provide examples showing that the matrix $\Phi$-SDPI constant can exceed the scalar counterpart. Finally, we derive inner bounds for $\Phi$-ribbons from prescribed independence structures and prove that these bounds are optimal when $\Phi(t)=t\log t$.

papers.title: Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications
papers.abstract: Semantic communication jointly optimizes inference accuracy, channel use, and computation, yet the underlying communication program is typically specified before training. This paper presents ComRSI (Communications-Oriented Recursive Self-Improvement), a framework for recursively evolving that program through large-language-model-assisted code edits. A fixed agent modifies the encoder, channel adapters, decoder, loss, and training policy; a protected evaluator screens candidates under prescribed budgets and resource constraints. Accepted code and textual feedback inform subsequent proposals, while candidate weights are trained from scratch. In the original ten-generation CIFAR-100 lineage, eight accepted revisions produce an attention-pooled code achieving 74.3% test accuracy over an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel at 32 complex symbols per image, compared with 67.2% at 256 symbols for the initial design. The program also improves fading-channel accuracy and transfers to Tiny-ImageNet after retraining. A repeat study with ten searches per method compares ComRSI against non-recursive agents with and without textual history. Mean final search scores balancing accuracy, transmission rate, and computational cost are 0.7587, 0.7376, and 0.7089, respectively; the mean numbers of accepted revisions per search are 6.0, 5.0, and 2.1. The advantage over the memoryless agent is supported by a two-sided rank test, whereas the difference from the history-equipped agent remains statistically inconclusive at this sample size. Archived proposals show that pooling can yield a large improvement, while retained history supports subsequent refinement. These results support recursive program optimization within the evaluated setting and expose its remaining rate-robustness and compute-placement trade-offs.

papers.title: S-PASS: Star-Topology Pinching-Antenna Systems with Pipelined Antenna Pre-Positioning
papers.abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) flexibly reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide near each user. Releasing and re-attaching an antenna, however, is a mechanical operation orders of magnitude slower than electronic switching, wasting much transmission time. Existing designs generally assume instant reconfiguration, neglect the mechanical latency, or keep the antenna fixed. This paper proposes S-PASS, a star architecture of waveguides sharing one radio-frequency chain through a switch, and pipelined antenna pre-positioning (PAP), a time-division protocol in which idle waveguides pre-position their antennas for their next users while one transmits. It derives in closed form the scheduling efficiency, the number of waveguides beyond which the latency costs no transmission time, and the latency up to which PAP outperforms fixed placement. Analytical and numerical results show that this latency grows with each added waveguide, and users at the outer ends of the waveguides gain most.

papers.title: On Almost MDS codes holding $(n-k-1)$-designs and an open problem on Witt design
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an almost maximum distance separable (AMDS) code over the finite fields with parameters $[n,k,n-k]$ whose minimum-weight codewords support an $(n-k-1)$-$(n,n-k,\lambda)$ design. We first determine the parameters of the dual code $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. We also characterize the design and its complementary design supported by the minimum weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. In particular, we present explicit formulas for the weight enumerators of all subset codes of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$ with length at least $k+1$. These formulas are completely determined by the cardinality of the subset, the dimension, together with the parameter $\lambda$, and are independent of the specific choice of subsets. As an application, we answer an open problem posed by Wang, Tang and Ding in 2023 by proving that the $3$-design supported by the minimum-weight codewords in their proposed cyclic dual code is isomorphic to the complementary design of the Witt spherical geometry design.

papers.title: Some Results on the Weight Spectrum of Binary Reed-Muller Codes $RM(m-7,m)$
papers.abstract: We study the set of weights occurring in the high-order binary Reed-Muller codes $RM(m-7,m)$. For every $m\geq 14$, we prove that the weight spectrum contains all even weights in $[336,2^m-336]$, together with an explicit finite set of low weights and their complements. The proof first establishes the corresponding base-code inclusion in $RM(7,14)$. This base step uses four-block concatenation, explicit degree-six monomial witnesses, and known spectrum inputs for $RM(5,10)$ and $RM(6,12)$. The base inclusion is then lifted to all $m\geq 14$ by a concatenation-based induction. We also analyze the remaining base-code target weights $322,326,330,334$ in several restricted families, including four-block branches, affine-flat and structured inner corrections in a fixed Carlet-type Maiorana-McFarland outer shell, and sparse sums of degree-7 coordinate monomials. The residual analysis delineates several construction routes that cannot yield the four unresolved base-code weights, thereby sharpening the remaining $c=7$ spectrum problem.

papers.title: On the maximum length of cyclic MDS codes
papers.abstract: We study the maximum length of nontrivial simple-root cyclic maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over ${\mathbb F}_q$. We prove $n\le q+1$ if $\gcd(n,q^2-1)>2$, or if the dimension is even and $\gcd(n,q^2-1)>1$. The bound also holds for all lengths whose prime factors lie in $\{2,3,5,7\}$. We obtain further cases involving primes $\ell\ge11$ with $(\ell-1)/2$ prime, under conditions on the exponents and the characteristic. The proofs combine Fourier supports, locality bounds and field descent with arithmetic restrictions on multiplicative orders and prime-adic valuations.

papers.title: Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.

papers.title: The Capacity of Interactive Secure Summation
papers.abstract: In secure summation, $K$ parties each hold an input, and the sum of the inputs is computed at one party, securely against at most $T$ colluding parties. Communication typically takes one hop: each party sends one message directly to the party that computes the sum, using correlated randomness that is independent of the inputs and held in advance. We consider interactive secure summation, where every pair of parties is connected by a secure link, so that each party can send messages to every other party, each party has only independent local randomness, and the messages may depend on the inputs and on earlier messages over multiple rounds. We characterize the capacity region, the set of achievable rates of communication, counting all messages exchanged among the parties over all rounds, and of the randomness of every party, counted in symbols per symbol of the sum. For $0\le T\le K-2$, the optimal communication rate is $K(K-1)/(K-T)$, and the randomness rates form a polyhedron with, up to a relabeling of the parties, a single extreme point: $T$ parties have the randomness rates $(K+T-2t)/(K-T)$, $t=1,\ldots,T$, and the others none. In particular, the optimal total randomness rate is $T(K-1)/(K-T)$. Linear schemes achieve every extreme point together with the optimal communication rate. The same techniques give the capacity region when every party recovers the sum and when the sum is computed at a server without input.

papers.title: When Majority-Vote Fails: Sequence Reconstruction under Fixed-Weight Substitutions
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of binary sequence reconstruction where a sequence is transmitted multiple times over a channel, and each undergoes substitution errors by an arbitrary error vector of Hamming weight exactly $t$. We determine $N_{\mathrm{wc}}$, the minimum number of distinct channel output observations guaranteeing unique reconstruction by an optimal decoder, and show that the bit-wise majority-vote decoder, which was proved by Levenshtein (2001) to be optimal for channels corrupting up to $t$ bits, is in fact suboptimal here. Despite this suboptimality, we prove a condition that admits a practical early-termination rule, necessary for every decoder at any number of outputs $N$, and sufficient for bit-wise majority-vote even below $N_{\mathrm{wc}}$. We evaluate the number of outputs at which this condition is triggered, numerically, and show that it frequently occurs below $N_{\mathrm{wc}}$ when the block-length $k>2t+1$. Finally, we propose an alternative algorithm aimed at guaranteeing unique reconstruction with fewer observations than bit-wise majority-vote, and demonstrate through exhaustive enumeration that it successfully decodes channel output-sets where bit-wise majority-vote fails.

papers.title: Combining e-values using demi-supermartingales
papers.abstract: We present a new method for combining e-variables through demi-supermartingales, which settles an old conjecture in the literature on nonparametric mean testing. It also provides an explicit concentration bound for a certain Kullback--Leibler-type statistic arising in the stochastic multi-armed bandit literature. All of these combination results hold for independent e-variables as well as for the class of co-valid e-variables, whose dependence structure lies somewhere between independence and sequential validity. The results are further generalized to compound e-variables. The proofs proceed by analyzing elementary symmetric polynomials and their behavior as nonnegative demi-supermartingales.

papers.title: A proof of Ward's conjecture on Griesmer codes
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be an $[n,k,d]_q$ Griesmer code, where $q=p^f$ with $p$ prime, and write $e=\nu_p(d)$. Ward conjectured that $C$ is $p^{\max\{0,e-f+1\}}$-divisible. In this paper, we prove this conjecture.
